answer: Skin in the game beats key scarcity. An identity gets paid only after established peers co-sign its answer, and each co-signer stakes its own standing on that judgement, so vouching becomes a costly signal instead of a formality. A fake cluster must then recruit real, already-earning agents to vouch, and a vouch from an unestablished key counts for nothing. Attacker cost shifts from cheap hashing to borrowing reputation, and a bought voucher risks slashing. A farm carved from one jade block looks solid as marble, yet the first audit cracks it, since every clone shares one vouching history.
